properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 23 at 4:04PM PST until November 25 at 6:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate
coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 8 to 12 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the
Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected.
For the High Surf Warning, large damaging breaking waves of 15
to 22 feet with dangerous rip currents are expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST
Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Wednesday
to noon PST Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 AM
Wednesday to noon PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beaches (especially Oceano Dunes,
Pismo Beach, Morro Bay, and Guadalupe Dunes), roads, and
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers
(including Cayucos, Avila, and Pismo) and jetties. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Large breaking waves
may impact Morro Bay Harbor. Extremely high tides may cause dock
damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of
harbor areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 7.7-8.2 feet will
likely peak between 7am and 11am. Coastal Flood and High Surf
Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of the
respective warnings.
properties.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 23 at 4:04PM PST until November 26 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 10 feet
with dangerous rip currents. Conditions will be worse west of
Point Conception, including Jalama Beach with large breaking
waves of 15 to 20 feet and moderate to significant coastal
flooding possible.

* WHERE...Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast and Santa
Barbara County Southeastern Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until noon PST
Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Wednesday to
noon PST Thursday.

vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time

damage is unlikely but possible. There is an increased risk for
ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out
to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Extremely
high tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low
lying areas inside of harbor areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Greater impacts are expected west of Point
Conception, with damaging flooding of sea water likely over
some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
time of high tide, including over beaches and beach parking
lots. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful waves and
strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean
drowning and damage to coastal structures like jetties. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Extremely high tides
of 8.1-8.5 feet will likely peak between 7am and 11am.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 23 at 2:34PM PST until November 26 at 2:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides
will cause major flooding in low lying areas mainly around
Humboldt Bay. Up to 3 of saltwater inundation above ground level
is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways. Between 10.3 and 11.0 feet MLLW at the North Spit
tide gauge is predicted. For the Coastal Flood Watch, High
astronomical tides and large surf may cause major flooding in
low lying areas along the Redwood Coast. Up to 2.5 foot of
saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying
areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 AM to 1 PM PST
Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday morning
through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at 11:09 AM on
Wednesday and 11:56 AM on Thursday at the Humboldt Bay North
Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2
hours before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
These impacts will include, but not limited to, roadways and
houses in King Salmon and the Arcata bottoms. This may also
include highway 101 near College of the Redwoods and Hwy 255
near the Mad River Slough. Shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The water levels from this are expected to
exceed the water levels seen in January of 2026 that caused
significant flooding in King Salmon.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that flooding is occurring or
imminent. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

morning's high tide. Breaking waves may reach 4-6 feet with
local sets up to 7-8 feet on west-facing beaches. Surf lowers
to 3-5 feet by Friday morning's high tide.
